faults.label: PA1 a block's start drops the remainder (the last n % W tasks of a job are in no block and never run)
PA2 each block ends one task past the next block's start (the task between them runs twice, the last block's one past the job's last task)
PA3 no worker takes another's leftovers (a worker held in a task leaves the rest of its block unrun)
PA4 a worker takes leftovers only from the next worker's block (with three or more workers the others' rests wait for their owners)
PA5 the blocks deal the head's tasks too (a led job's leading tasks, and every task of a job no larger than its workers, run twice)
PA6 no worker claims the head's tasks (a led job's leading tasks, and every task of a job no larger than its workers, never run)
PA7 the blocks dealt over the pool's threads, not the job's cap (the blocks of workers past the cap never run)
PA8 a claim of the head takes two tasks (every other leading task never runs)
PA9 the leftovers' check inverted (a worker skips every other block that still has tasks)
faults.new: if (k && __atomic_load_n(&b->next,__ATOMIC_RELAXED)<b->end) continue;  /* nothing left in it */
faults.old: if (k && __atomic_load_n(&b->next,__ATOMIC_RELAXED)>=b->end) continue;  /* nothing left in it */

faults.label: PA10 a head past the job's tasks kept (the blocks' share wraps below zero: tasks past the job's last run)
PA11 the blocks' room missing (the workers' counters past the first written beyond the bytes the pool asked for)
